title: Over a Noetherian local ring of depth zero an injective map of finite free modules has a unit maximal minor
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] whose maximal ideal is an associated prime of $R$: there is $z\in R$ with $\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak m$. Let $n,p\ge0$ be integers and $A$ a $p\times n$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix] such that the $R$-linear map $R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus p}$, $v\mapsto Av$, between free modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] is injective. Then $n\le p$, and some $n\times n$ minor of $A$, i.e. the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the $n\times n$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] of $A$ formed by $n$ of its rows, is a unit of $R$ (for $n=0$ the empty minor is $1$). Equivalently, the ideal of $R$ generated by the $n\times n$ minors of $A$ is $R$.

proof.text:
(Set-up.) Fix $z\in R$ with $\{a\in R:az=0\}=\mathfrak m$. Since $1
otin\mathfrak m$ we have $1\cdot z
eq0$, so $z
eq0$. Let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, a field [def-weil-field] because $\mathfrak m$ is a maximal ideal, and $a\mapsto ar a$ the quotient map, a ring homomorphism. Write $ ar A=( ar a_{ij})$ for the $p	imes n$ matrix over $\kappa$ obtained by reducing every entry of $A=(a_{ij})$ [def-weil-matrix]. For $a\in R$: $za=0$ iff $a\in\mathfrak m$, by the choice of $z$.

proof.text: ($\bar A$ is injective.) Let $\bar w\in\kappa^n$ with $\bar A\bar w=0$; we show $\bar w=0$. Choose $w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in R^{\oplus n}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] lifting $\bar w$ coordinatewise. Every coordinate $(Aw)_i=\sum_j a_{ij}w_j$ reduces to $(\bar A\bar w)_i=0$, so $(Aw)_i\in\mathfrak m$ and hence $z(Aw)_i=0$ (Step 1). Therefore $A(zw)=z\,(Aw)=0$, and injectivity of $v\mapsto Av$ gives $zw=0$, i.e. $zw_j=0$ for every $j$. By Step 1, $w_j\in\mathfrak m$, i.e. $\bar w_j=0$, for every $j$. So $\bar w=0$, and the $\kappa$-linear map $\kappa^n\to\kappa^p$, $\bar v\mapsto\bar A\bar v$, is injective. (This is the argument of the source: $x f_1$ is not mapped to zero, so some matrix coefficient is not in $\mathfrak m$; here it is applied to every vector at once.)

proof.text: (A nonzero maximal minor over $\kappa$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-field-injective-matrix-nonzero-maximal-minor] applied to the field $\kappa$ and the matrix $B=\bar A$, injective by Step 2: $n\le p$, and there is $S=\{i_1<\dots<i_n\}\subseteq\{1,\dots,p\}$ with $\det(\bar A_S)\neq0$ in $\kappa$, where $\bar A_S$ is the $n\times n$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] of $\bar A$ on the rows $S$. This proves $n\le p$.

proof.text:
(The minor is a unit.) Let $A_S$ be the $n	imes n$ submatrix of $A$ on the rows $S$; its reduction entrywise is $ ar A_S$. The determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] is the polynomial expression $\det M=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_k M_{\sigma(k),k}$ in the entries with integer coefficients $\pm1$, and $a\mapsto ar a$ is a ring homomorphism, so $\overline{\det(A_S)}=\det( ar A_S)
eq0$, i.e. $\det(A_S)
otin\mathfrak m$ (for $n=0$ both sides are $1$). In the local ring $R$ an element $d
otin\mathfrak m$ is a unit: otherwise $dR$ is a proper ideal, contained in some maximal ideal, which is $\mathfrak m$ since $\mathfrak m$ is the only maximal ideal, so $d\in\mathfrak m$. Hence the $n	imes n$ minor $\det(A_S)$ of $A$ is a unit of $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MY (lemma-exact-depth-zero-local, line 24678), proof (the element x with m x = 0 and the matrix coefficient not in m)

proof.text: (The ideal of minors.) Let $I$ be the ideal generated by the $n\times n$ minors of $A$. By Step 4, $I$ contains the unit $\det(A_S)$, so $I=R$. Conversely, if $I=R$ then not all generators lie in $\mathfrak m$ (otherwise $I\subseteq\mathfrak m\neq R$), so some $n\times n$ minor lies outside $\mathfrak m$ and is a unit as in Step 4; so the two formulations of the conclusion are equivalent.
